title: Arnautovic dropped by West Ham, team news and transfer latest – as it happened
trail: Cardiff signed a striker (on loan) and various other things also happened as the world counted down to another thrill-packed weekend
byline: Simon Burnton (now) and John Brewin (over lunch)
body: And with that I’m going to wrap things up. It’s been another splendid day of non-stop action. Thanks for being with me, and have a great weekend. Bye! Claude Puel’s short-term future would be rendered considerably rosier should Leicester get three points from this match: This morning I mentioned that Levante had appealed to have Barcelona expelled from the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player against them in the last round. The case has now been decided in Barcelona’s favour on a technicality - Levante didn’t submit their appeal within the 48-hour deadline for these things - and the quarter-finals have been drawn with them still in it. “After studying the complaint and the corresponding allegations, the head of the competition has decided to maintain the result of the tie and keep Barcelona in the quarter-final draw,” the federation said. And here is that draw: Real Madrid v Gerona Getafe v Valencia Sevilla v Barcelona Espanyol v Real Betis The Friday Fiver has landed! Jurgen Klopp has said Rhian Brewster is not in his plans for the remainder of the season as the young Liverpool striker continues his rehabilitation from ankle and knee surgery. The highly-rated 18-year-old has been sidelined for 12 months having damaged ankle ligaments and his meniscus in an under-23s game against Manchester City. Brewster was pictured running at Melwood earlier this week but an impending return to competitive action was ruled out on Friday by Klopp, who insists there is no need to rush the England Under-17 World Cup winner’s recovery. “He’s not as far as he would like to be,” the Liverpool manager said. “He’s outside training, his running looks much better since he had this other little surgery. He’s in a good way but it will take time. But it’s no problem, he has the time. “We don’t have to think about him before the pre-season, I would say. He’s in a good mood. He’s a nice fella, really integrated in the team, but so far he couldn’t show it on the pitch. But our opinion about him will not change. We have to wait a little longer for him.” Klopp provided a more positive update on Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain who, like Brewster, has not featured this season due to serious knee injury. The manager added: “He’s closer than Rhian, he’s on a very good way but it will still take time. Last time, I think I put a bit of pressure on the medical department but when I see him running or on the ball, it looks good, promising, close to return. No problems, no swellings, he can work on his fitness issues. I think we will see him this season.” Stuart James has written about Claude Puel’s position at Leicester City, why it’s under threat and precisely how much threat it’s under: Another week, another audience with Leicester City’s manager, and another question about his future. “It’s a common thread, all press conferences, I cannot manage these rumours,” Claude Puel replied, smiling. “It’s often we have a lot of bets about my future. But I’m sorry for lots of people who made this bet because they lost a lot of money.” Puel remains the favourite to be the next Premier League manager to leave his job, which may come as a surprise to those whose knowledge of Leicester begins and ends with their position in the table: eighth. The assumption that tends to follow is that any disgruntled Leicester supporters have ideas above their station, fuelled by that 5,000-1 triumph three years ago, and now expect to challenge for the title every season. The truth is rather different and has more to do with what they are paying to watch. To put it bluntly – and many Southampton supporters will probably be nodding their heads when they get to the end of this sentence – the football at home has been dull under Puel on far too many occasions to remember. Much more here: John Vickers, the former general manager of Lincoln City, has been sentenced to 14 months in prison for fraud. He admitted to defrauding the club of £35,000, which he said in court was used to fund a gambling addiction. This is the club’s statement: Lincoln City Football Club unequivocally condemn the actions of Mr John Vickers which have resulted in today’s sentencing. John Vickers was a trusted employee, work colleague and friend of many at Lincoln City Football Club for a number of years so the discovery of his actions was met with feelings of shock and disappointment. In closing we would like to thank the authorities for their diligence in their investigations. Lincoln City Football Club are pleased to learn this matter as now been concluded and as such will be making no further comment. I have been watching Sky Sports News for seven hours now. Apart from adverts for Over-50s health insurance, the thing I’ve seen repeated most often is the assertion that Gonzalo Higuain’s brother and agent is poised to board a flight to England to discuss and complete a move to Chelsea. Latest is that he’s still waiting. Nuno Espirito Santo has been talking about his approach to the midseason transfer window: I agree that it’s more difficult to sign players in January. You don’t have the same numbers of players available. It doesn’t make sense to bring someone in that you don’t find different to what you already have. The other point is knowing what you sometimes want, or the profile you want, is not available in the transfer window because they are doing well in other teams and they don’t want to sell. It’s the same as us. If someone comes knocking on my door and asks for some kind of player, the answer will be ‘no’, because we are building, we are trying to maintain the core, and other teams have the same approach, so it becomes very hard to make deals during this transfer window. The transfer window is here, but to bring someone that we find appropriate takes a lot of thinking and there are lots of decisions to make. At the same time, all the names that have been linked to us is a guessing game for journalists, trying to guess players who are not true. The way we work is clear; myself, my team and my players are only focused on the game and the club is prepared to act if we think that’s the best decision we have. News from Bolton, where John McGinlay, who scored over 100 goals during a five-year spell at the club in the 1990s and is widely cherished as a club legend, has been banned from reporting on their game against West Brom. In an interview a couple of weeks ago he was asked about the club’s current state. “It’s an embarrassment,” he said. “It’s a disgrace the way this club has been run.” His criticism of the club’s ownership has been cited as a reason for the decision. Here’s Roy Hodgson on the prospect of fielding Julian Speroni at Anfield. Speroni would become the first player born in the 1970s to play in the Premier League this season, and perhaps the last player born in that decade ever to play in the English top flight (at least until I inherit a fortune from my long lost uncle Bob, buy a club and force the manager to give me a runout): It’s a tough ask, there’s no question of that. In an ideal world you’d not be thrusting him in, you’d hopefully be easing him in, but we’ve no choice. He’s happy to have the chance and I’m pretty sure he’ll be working very hard to make certain he stays in contention, even when the other two are fit. But that hasn’t bothered me particularly. Julian is a very, very active goalkeeper, certainly in training. I don’t notice any difference in him from when he played a year ago; I’m happy that we’ve got him. He’s looking forward to it, has confidence in himself. He’s a good goalkeeper, so we’re very fortunate. To have his quality and experience as the third goalkeeper is pretty fortunate. We’ve someone who’s played over 400 times for Palace and is in very good shape. And a news story from Jacob Steinberg on Marko Arnautovic’s ongoing rabid strop: A couple more match previews for your delectation. Firstly, Brighton’s visit to Old Trafford: And secondly, Burnley’s trip to Vicarage Road: What a team this was. Generally the 5-0 win over Nottingham Forest the previous year is considered their high point, but the 9-0 victory over Crystal Palace, which happened 30 years ago, wasn’t bad either: As Palace head back to Anfield, Steven Pye has written a thing about that game. And here it is! We all miss this guy, don’t we? He hopes to be back soon, and here’s video evidence: Here’s Rafael Benitez on the chances of Newcastle bringing new players in this month: Everything is depending on what you have done previously. You have to keep working for the summer window, and after keep working for the January window. This is more difficult because you have less players available, but still there are good players that maybe you can get. It’s about the right player at the right time. We are working for a while [on potential signings], and we’ll still keep working. It has now been confirmed that Marko Arnautovic will not be in the West Ham squad to face Bournemouth, because he’s too unsettled: Mauricio Pochettino says Tottenham might sign someone this month, but probably won’t: We are open to improving our squad, to add players that can improve us, but it is not going to put pressure on us to sign players. We know very well the market is very difficult. If we identify a player who is going to help us, identify the player that can add quality we don’t have in the squad, we are more than open to try. But at the moment, I think there’s not too many possibilities to add the kind of player that can improve us. There’s many names that appear in every transfer window. With Gonzalo Higuain apparently incoming, will the match at Arsenal be the last time Eden Hazard is asked to play as false nine? The league leaders host Crystal Palace tomorrow. Here’s a preview: And here’s birthday boy Pep Guardiola on the search for a backup/replacement for Fernandinho: The way we play we need a guy with physicality, quick in the head, the reading, with our spaces to attack. As many things he can do, the better. It’s not easy to find one player who can do everything, and the price and the agents and the clubs ... So we will see. We have seen three, four players we are looking for. We will check if we can do it. Here’s Mauricio Pochettino on life without Harry Kane: Harry is a very positive person, the moment he got injured he started thinking about recovering as soon as possible. When he is one of the best strikers in Europe it is going to affect performances. We are positive we can cope and we have players who can cover his position. It won’t affect our approach to the games. Rafael Benitez has clarified the situation regarding Newcastle’s injury list, ahead of their crucial home game against Cardiff: “I’m more or less optimistic. We have more or less the same problems we had. The new problems, we will decide tomorrow. But I am quite optimistic with Hayden, with Schar, with Clark, with Lascelles. I think they can be available if everything is fine.” Of course if everything is not fine, they won’t be. So, that’s cleared up then. Claudio Ranieri has clarified the nature of the widely-discussed yoga-related bust-up between Aleksandar Mitrovic and Aboubakar Kamara: It wasn’t a battle, it was a chat. Apparently it was “something that happens in every team”. So there you go. Nothing to see here. Everyone is being asked about Marcelo Bielsa today. Here’s Pep Guardiola’s response: No manager around the world works with the amount of information that he has. It’s unique in the world, how he works. But I think the most important, what I learned about what he said is that football belongs to the players. In the end, the players make the difference. And that’s what I most agree with from what he said. The Crystal Palace manager, Roy Hodgson, has just confirmed that Julian Speroni, 39-year-old goalkeeper and former restaurateur (Speroni’s used to be advertised on team sheets, but shut down in 2016), will start at Liverpool tomorrow. He last played a game for Palace on December 28 2017. Today saw the unveiling of a West Midlands tram, named in honour of the late, great Cyrille Regis, who died a year ago this week. Forget your ten-year challenges, how about some real nostalgia from the Nessun Dorma podcast crew? More Sarri, from the Press Association wire. Remember, though, he doesn’t have much to do with the actual nuts and bolts of deals, even if Jorginho is clearly his player and Higuaín is another of his former Napoli players. Maurizio Sarri on Friday refused to be drawn on the prospect of Gonzalo Higuaín joining Chelsea, with the Blues head coach insisting he is not spending his energy on transfers. Higuaín, who is on loan at AC Milan from Juventus, has been linked with a reunion with Sarri, who was his boss at Napoli. Asked how close Higuaín was to signing, Sarri said: “I don’t know. I want to be clear, because I cannot help you.” The Chelsea manager Maurizio Sarri has been asked - of course he has - about Marcelo Bielsa’s spy missions. In Italy, yes [it happened]. I prefer to study my opponents by video. It is difficult to have a lot of information in the last two days, so I don’t like this. Every coach tries to have information about the opponents, but I don’t like the way. It happened a bit in Italy. I am not a very good spy. José Mourinho news, or at least Rui Faria news. The Lowry lingerer’s bagman/attack dog/former assistant has finally got his first management job. From the wires: Doha (AFP) – Rui Faria, an assistant to Jose Mourinho at a number of Europe’s biggest teams, has become head coach at Qatari league side Al Duhail, the club announced on Friday. Duhail said it made an agreement with Faria “to be the coach of the team in the upcoming period”. “The club will present its new coach to the media in a major press conference that will be announced in the upcoming two days,” the club said on its website. Let us recall the kind, almost poetic, words the master had for his apprentice when Rui took his leave of Manchester last summer. 17 years… in Leiria, Porto, London, Milan, Madrid, London again and Manchester. Training, playing, travelling, studying, laughing and also a few tears of happiness. 17 years and the kid is now a man. The intelligent student is now a football expert, ready for a successful career as a manager.I will miss my friend and that is the hardest thing for me, but his happiness is more important and, of course, I respect his decision, especially because I know that we will always be together. Be happy, brother! Quiz! Quiz! Quiz! And this week’s is a toughie. Mark Hudson is Huddersfield Town’s stand-in manager, and gave a press conference this morning ahead of what seems likely to be only game in charge, Sunday’s meeting with Manchester City. Rumours in Germany suggest another Borussia Dortmund coach will be coming in: Jan Siewert, coach of the Under-23s. Anyway, Hudson and captain Tommy Smith have thrown a bit of light on David Wagner’s departure. First, Smith. We probably heard a little bit before you did. It’s certainly been a shock to all of us. Our first reaction was disappointment. This manager has done a hell of a lot for this football club. There was shock, disappointment, but ultimately, we move on. We have to win the match on Sunday...He didn’t say anything. I was in the dressing room after the game and it was no different to any other. The atmosphere was down, but no one realised what was going to happen. Next, Hudson He has brought everyone together in the community. Everyone should fully respect what he has done here. I will still be in contact with him. I have learned a lot from him as a player and a manager. He came in in the morning and said his goodbyes. You create real relationships and bonds so yes it was emotional. He said thanks to the players for everything they have given to him and I said the same to him. He knows what I’m like and he knows I’ve got a job to do so I said thank you and that I would be in contact. We have 16 games to give everything we have. We will not leave any stone unturned and will fight for everything on the pitch. That’s what we will do. Harry Pearson on one of football’s continuing rituals is well worth a read. Here’s a Bournemouth v West Ham preview, which I shall leave you to enjoy for a bit. John Brewin will take you through the lunch gap. Important Manchester property update: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer won’t be at the Lowry Hotel quite as long as Jose Mourinho: I’m still in the hotel but I’ve found a place, so I won’t be too long. I’ve been driving around a bit to find my bearings again. I’ve got mates here, so I have been to see a few of them so it’s not like I’m stuck in the hotel on my own. We await developments in the tale of Chelsea’s pursuit of Gonzalo Higuain, which apparently could be concluded today. In the meantime, a little further down the pyramid, somewhat less high-profile transfers are happening... Check out your Cech knowledge, and also other stuff, in the sports quiz of the week: The match previews are starting to drop. Here’s the first, which will cover all your Southampton v Everton needs: I’m hearing that Marko Arnautovic is a doubt for West Ham’s trip to Bournemouth tomorrow. There’s uncertainty over whether the forward is in the right frame of mind after West Ham rejected a £35m bid from a Chinese club for him last week. It’s a difficult situation for Manuel Pellegrini, who won’t want to be without his first choice striker against Bournemouth. However Arnautovic is said to be unhappy at West Ham’s refusal to budge. He might have to suck it up, though. West Ham don’t have much time to find a replacement this month. They’ve looked at Celta Vigo’s Maxi Gómez, but the 22-year-old Uruguayan won’t be cheap. Sala’s imminent move to Cardiff appears to have set the cat among the Nantes-based pigeons. According to French media (such as this article in L’Equipe), Vahid Halilhodzic, the Bosnian manager who joined the club only in October, might end up leaving in protest. Here’s Eddie Howe on rumours surrounding Callum Wilson and a potential move to either Chelsea or West Ham, and on transfers in general: I don’t want to place any more pressure on Callum or any of my players in my team by talking about things that aren’t important really. What’s important for me is Callum working hard for the team, producing his best performances and on a consistent basis. For him, thinking about transfer fees, values and other clubs, I would recommend that he focuses on Bournemouth and our games to come. We’ve had no interest in any of our players, everything has just been speculation, which you understand, this is the month for it, and I am sure it will not be the last thing that we hear. I think from my perspective and the team we have above me, we are always working together to try to find solutions to make the team better, the squad stronger and make the team continue to go forward. They are the main things. Here’s photographic evidence of Oumar Niasse’s move to Cardiff: Here’s a piece on the state of play in the Bundesliga: The Bundesliga restarts after the winter break on Friday with something very unfamiliar yet extremely tantalising on the horizon: a proper title race. Borussia Dortmund lead the German league at the halfway point by six points from Bayern Munich, with Borussia Mönchengladbach a further three behind. This is unusual, to say the least. Bayern have been the Herbsmeister (autumn champions) for the past seven years and have won every league title since 2012-13. This time, though, they are the hunters and it is a role the Bayern players are enjoying. More here: Some news from Spain now, courtesy of Reuters: Levante have filed a complaint to the Spanish football federation (RFEF) stating that Barcelona fielded an ineligible player in their Copa del Rey last-16, first-leg match, the La Liga side said in a statement on Twitter on Friday. If the RFEF rule against Barca, who deny breaking any rules, they would be thrown out of the Copa, which they have won for the last four years, with Levante taking their place in the quarter-finals. The last-eight draw is due to take place at 5pm local time on Friday. Levante say that the Barça defender Juan ‘Chumi’ Brandáriz was ineligible to play in the game on 10 January, which Levante won 2-1, as he was serving a suspension for Barça’s B team, which he had earned in a Spanish third-tier game. Neil Warnock has now confirmed that Niasse has signed for Cardiff on loan from Everton for the remainder of this season: The Niasse deal’s done. I’m relieved because I thought it was done yesterday. So to find out this morning is something I could have done without, but it’s nice to know that he’s available. Sala will apparently sign a three-and-a-half year contract, with Oumar Niasse also coming on loan. In his press conference Marco Silva mentioned Niasse as one of Everton’s forward options, “if he doesn’t leave”. If Sala is to feature in tomorrow’s match in Newcastle, his transfer must be registered with the Premier League in the next 67 minutes. And news of a transfer apparently about to happen: Sky are reporting that Emiliano Sala is in Cardiff right now, having his medical ahead of an £18m move from Nantes. In case you missed them, here are today’s big rumours: And here’s Jamie Jackson’s take on Solskjaer’s press conference: Here’s some more from Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, on whether his side might be a tad overconfident against Brighton having won their last six games: Overconfident? No, you cannot be too confident. Confidence is one thing, complacency is the other side of it, that you think it’s going to be easy. I want players to be confident, but I don’t want them to be complacent and take their foot off the pedal because that’s a big difference for me. I want them going into the games full of confidence taking people on, playing, running, passing forward, getting the crowd with them, because that’s what it’s about. Good news for Burnley: they had a shot on target against Fulham after all! Today’s Premier League birthday news: Pep Guardiola is 48 today, and Chelsea’s Robert Green is 39. Some news from Leicester, where Marc Albrighton has signed a new contract that will (might) keep him at the club until 2022. This is what he said about it: It was totally straightforward. Leicester offered me a deal and I was always going to sign it. I’ve had some good times here and hopefully I can continue to do so. When I first signed, I looked at the squad that was in the dressing room and the Club itself in terms of its fanbase and what sort of club it was. It was a family Club back then and it’s a family Club now. It’s something that suits me down to the ground. It really fit in well with me as a person and it’s the perfect fit for me. Here’s Marco Silva, who implies that he will keep playing Richarlison at centre-forward despite a five-game goal drought: My aim as a coach and a manager is to put the starting XI on the pitch and the XI I think is the best solution for each match. Richarlison can play out wide or as a striker; now he is playing more as a striker. I know every three or four matches he doesn’t score the same conversation will come again. I know he hasn’t scored since Boxing Day but he is a possibility to play as a striker, and I will decide the best solution as to who will play in that position. What I can say is he feels as comfortable in that position as he does playing out wide, it is the same for him, and it is up to us to decide. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer has delivered an update on Manchester United’s preparations for tomorrow’s home game against Brighton. The big news: BONG! Alexis Sanchez is available! He’s champing at the bit, I have to say. He’s working hard in training. His attitude in training has been fantastic and he wants to play, so I’m looking forward to seeing him. But I’ve got loads of good players to choose from. BONG! Marouane Fellaini is not available! He’ll probably be [out] at least three or four weeks. He’s got a calf problem and that’s sad because there’s X factors in different players and we all know Felli’s X factor. Then again, he’ll be working hard to get back in when all the big games are coming as well. So the weekend is nearly here, and with it an avalanche of winter football, including key clashes towards the top and the bottom of the Premier League. Let’s start with the weekend’s English top-flight fixtures, and then take it from there: Saturday (3pm unless stated) Arsenal v Chelsea (5.30pm) Bournemouth v West Ham Liverpool v Crystal Palace Manchester United v Brighton Newcastle United v Cardiff City Southampton v Everton Watford v Burnley Wolverhampton Wanderers v Leicester (12.30pm) Sunday Fulham v Tottenham (4pm) Huddersfield v Manchester City (1.30pm) And here are 10 things to look out for in those games: In other news: It’s a rest day in the Asian Cup. The Round of 16 starts on Sunday. There are games tonight in the Championship (Norwich v Birmingham), the Bundesliga (Hoffenheim v Bayern Munich) and in Ligue 1 (Lille v Amiens). A tram will be officially named after Cyrille Regis in Wednesbury at 11am. Welcome! Let’s see what the day throws at us, shall we?
